data.name: Eliathah
data.long_meaning: The Hebrew name Eliathah is derived from the Hebrew elements El (My God) and Yah (YHWH, the Hebrew name for God). It is a Hebrew name borne by several characters in the Old Testament. Eliathah is also the name of one of the sons of Saul and Rizpah (2 Samuel 21:8).
data.spiritual_meaning: Reflects one's deep faith and devotion to God.
data.numerology_meaning: A loving, caring, and nurturing soul with a deep sense of responsibility.

in_hebrew.name: אליעתה
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא האל שלי, ה' הוא המושיע שלי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אליעתה הוא שם פרטי עברי המורכב מ'אל' ו'יעתה', שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא האל שלי' או 'ה' הוא המושיע שלי'. השם מופיע בתנ'ך, ביחזקאל ובדברי הימים, ומשמעותו רוחנית ועמוקה, הקושרת בין האדם לאלוהים.

in_greek.name: Ελιαθας
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι ο Θεός μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Ελιαθας είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι ο Θεός μου' ή 'Ο Κύριος είναι ο σωτήρας μου'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοια ονόματα αναφέρονται ως σύμβολο της πίστης και της αφοσίωσης στον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Eliathah
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Eliathah origine Hebraeum est, quod interpretatur 'Deus est Deus meus' vel 'Dominus est salvator meus'. In traditione Christiana, nomina quae similia sunt, significant devotionem et fidem in Deum.

in_english.name: Eliathah
in_english.meaning: God is my God, the Lord is my savior
in_english.long_meaning: Eliathah originates from Hebrew 'El' (אל) meaning 'God' and 'Ya'tah' (יעתה) meaning 'my God' or 'savior'. Found in biblical references such as Chronicles, this name signifies a deep spiritual connection and devotion to God. Historically, it reflects the monotheistic beliefs of the Israelites and early Christians. The name symbolizes faith, spiritual strength, and divine protection.

biblical_reference.note: A leader of the Levites during David's reign.

data.cultural_impact: Eliathah is a name that reflects strong religious devotion and faith in God. It is a name that highlights the belief in the divine power and guidance of God in one's life. The name is also rooted in Jewish history and culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Eliathah signifies a strong connection with God and a deep belief in His power and guidance. It is a reminder of the faithfulness and providence of God in one's life. The name is also a reminder of the importance of trusting in God and relying on His strength and wisdom in times of need. Eliathah is a name that inspires faith, hope, and trust in the divine power of God.

historical_references.reference: According to the Old Testament book of 1 Samuel, Eliathah was a priest who ministered in the Tabernacle at Shiloh during the time of the judges. He is mentioned as the father of Iddo, who in turn was the father of the high priest Azariah during the reign of King Josiah of Judah (around 640 BCE).
historical_references.context: Pre-monarchic period of Israelite history, during the time of the judges.

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament apocryphal book of the Shepherd of Hermas, the name Eliathah is given to the angelic guide who leads the protagonist Hermas through a series of visions and interpretations of allegorical dreams. The book was likely written around the late 2nd century CE.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Eliathah is of biblical origin, derived from the Hebrew language meaning 'my God is abundance'. It is seen in modern contexts in academic research related to biblical studies, particularly in the context of the Old Testament. Additionally, it has gained interest in the field of Jewish genealogy as many individuals seek to trace their ancestral roots. Lastly, the name Eliathah has found a place in the realm of fantasy literature, where it may be used as a character name or place name in various works.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Eliathah, a minister in London, United Kingdom, shares that their name Eliathah meaning "My God is Yah" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

It is a reminder of God's presence and guidance in one's life, and the unwavering belief that He is always there as a source of strength and support.
